Consistency.justification: The proposal perfectly aligns with the provided research idea, accurately incorporating the multicore fiber Hartmann-like mask, angular memory effect, and speckle spectral decorrelation to address the single-shot spatio-spectral wavefront sensing problem. The literature review accurately identifies the gaps in current DOE, coded-pupil, and multimode fiber sensors, logically motivating the proposed approach.

Clarity.justification: The proposal is exceptionally well-structured and crystal clear. Every section, from the abstract to the detailed experimental setups, is concisely articulated. The breakdown of the forward model, reconstruction algorithms, baseline comparisons, and evaluation metrics leaves no ambiguity about how the research will be executed.

Novelty.justification: The integration of a multicore fiber into a Hartmann-style sensor to concurrently exploit the angular memory effect for spatial gradients and speckle decorrelation for spectral information is highly innovative. It offers a fresh and elegant optical design that elegantly merges wavefront sensing and speckle spectrometry into a single-shot framework.

Soundness.justification: The technical rigor of the proposal is outstanding. The forward model includes a comprehensive and highly realistic set of optical and detector nonidealities (PRNU, IPC, read noise, stray light). The commitment to Cramér-Rao Bound (CRB) analysis, Fisher Information-driven design, and thorough Monte Carlo simulations for correlated fabrication errors demonstrates a deep, quantitative understanding of computational imaging.

Feasibility.justification: The proposal presents a well-thought-out, staged experimental plan (synthetic -> SLM -> fabricated multicore fiber mask) that helps mitigate risks. However, fabricating, aligning, and, most importantly, maintaining the precise broadband spatio-spectral calibration of a multicore fiber mask over a wide aperture presents significant practical challenges. While the proposal acknowledges these risks (thermal drift, stability), physical realization will require considerable effort.

Significance.justification: Developing a compact, single-shot hyperspectral wavefront sensor would address a critical need in fields constrained by temporal resolution or photon budgets, such as adaptive optics, biomedical imaging, and astronomy. The rigorous theoretical framework (CRB and FI analysis) could also serve as a foundational methodology for future computational imaging systems.

strengths: Highly innovative optical concept combining angular memory effect and speckle spectrometry
Exceptionally rigorous forward modeling including realistic detector nonidealities and fabrication errors
Comprehensive evaluation plan grounded in information theory (CRB, Fisher Information) and Monte Carlo robustness analysis
weaknesses: Practical challenges and potential instability in physically coupling and calibrating the multicore fiber mask for broadband light
Computational complexity of the joint non-linear reconstruction algorithm may hinder real-time adaptive optics deployment
